title: India-Asia collision and rise of the Himalaya
summary: India, moving north after leaving Gondwana, collided with Asia along what is now the Yarlung Zangbo suture in Tibet, raising the Himalaya and Tibetan Plateau. Dating is disputed: one provenance study puts collision onset at about 59 million years ago, another near 55, with full collision around 40, and the US Geological Survey says 40 to 50 million years ago.

uncertainty.note: Onset 59 +/-1 Ma (Hu et al.) or 55 +/-5 Ma (SUSTech, rotation-based); complete collision 40 +/-5 Ma (SUSTech). USGS: roughly 40 to 50 Ma. Timing remains debated; the atlas id uses -50.

as_recorded.value: collision onset as middle Palaeocene (59 +/-1 Ma)
first contact around 55 +/-5 Ma; complete collision around 40 +/-5 Ma
India and Eurasia collided roughly 40 to 50 million years ago

where.modern_name: Lhasa, Tibet, China (proxy point on the Yarlung Zangbo suture zone)
where.historical_name: Yarlung Zangbo suture between the Indian plate and Eurasia (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point 29.65, 91.10 reconstructed to 55 Ma (mid-range of the 59-50 Ma onset estimates). PALEOMAP gives 14.99 N, 79.92 E.

importance.justification: Created the Himalaya and Tibetan Plateau, reshaping Asian climate, river systems and monsoon patterns.
